task.description: Review REQ-006's content per docs/agents/decisions/0002 — CONTENT-BA wrote real Cyrillic-script Kazakh translations directly into messages/kk.json (no CODE-DESIGNER step, per that decision). Review against content_ba_guide.md's voice/casing/vocabulary rules, all 5 of REQ-006's acceptance criteria (see CONTENT-BA's handoff at handoffs/WF02-REQ005-REQ006/step-07-content-ba.json for the full text), and scope (only messages/kk.json should have changed, no drive-by src/ edits). CONTENT-BA reports several ru/kk identical values claimed as legitimate untranslatable literals (names, codes, brand/URL tokens, city names) -- spot-check a sample yourself to confirm they're genuine exceptions, not missed translations. Also spot-check that the Kazakh prose reads as genuine Kazakh (not a mechanical Russian transliteration) -- you don't need fluency to sanity-check this: confirm Kazakh-specific letters actually appear distributed across many different keys (not clustered in only 2-3 places), which would suggest real translation rather than token-swapping a few words.
acceptance_criteria: git diff master...HEAD reviewed directly; scoped to messages/kk.json plus expected bookkeeping
Independent check that domain vocabulary terms use the exact stated casing/form with no synonym substitution
Independent check that status-label keys are plain lowercase Kazakh
Independent check that Metadata.ogLocale is exactly 'kk_KZ'
Independent check that Kazakh-specific letters (Ә/Ғ/Қ/Ң/Ө/Ұ/Ү/Һ/І) appear broadly distributed across the file, not clustered
Spot-check at least 5 of the claimed-identical-to-ru.json values to confirm they're legitimate untranslatable literals, not missed translations
FAIL if a genuine violation found; otherwise PASS with any non-blocking notes

result.summary: git diff master...HEAD confirmed scope: the REQ-006 commit (401080e) touched only messages/kk.json plus its own handoff file, as expected. Metadata.ogLocale is exactly 'kk_KZ'. Status-label keys (chapter{N}Status, stream{N}Status) are plain lowercase Kazakh with no exclamation marks/slogans/emoji anywhere in the file. Kazakh-specific letters (Ә/Ғ/Қ/Ң/Ө/Ұ/Ү/Һ/І) appear in 111/177 keys spread across all 13 namespaces (not clustered), confirming real translation work. Spot-checked 8 ru/kk-identical values (Metrics.metric1Source numeric, Events.talk1Who/talk1Role person name + country code, MapSection.nodeTashkentLabel city name, Streams.foundationLink URL, Footer.contactsTelegram handle, Footer.hashtag, Team.team1Role English role title) — all legitimate untranslatable literals, this part of CONTENT-BA's claim holds. BLOCKING VIOLATION FOUND: the domain-vocabulary rule was misapplied. The requirement's decision text says Event/Chapter/Talk/Speaker/CFP/etc. stay in English 'exactly as they already do in Russian... copy' -- but in messages/ru.json these words are actually translated (событие/события for 'event', чаптер/чаптеры for 'chapter', доклад for 'talk'); only CFP genuinely appears verbatim in English in ru.json (confirmed by regex scan: only Band.lede and Doors.door2Body match, both via CFP). Instead, messages/kk.json inserts the literal capitalized English words 'Event'/'Events'/'Chapter'/'Chapters'/'Talk' broadly, well beyond CFP: Nav.events='Events' (ru: 'События'), Nav.chapters='Chapters' (ru: 'Чаптеры'), Hero.ctaPrimary='Жақындағы Event' (ru: 'Ближайшее событие'), Band.lede='Келесі Event...' (ru: 'Следующее событие...'), Doors.door1Body='Жақындағы Event мен ел чатына тіркелу' (ru: 'ближайшее событие'), Doors.door2Link='Talk ұсыну →' (ru: 'Подать доклад →'), Events.eyebrow='Events' (ru: 'События'), Streams.stream1Title='Events' (ru: 'События'), Partners.partner1Desc='...Event залдары' (ru: '...залы для событий'), MapSection.ctaLaunchChapter='Өз қалаңызда Chapter ашу' (ru: 'Запустить чаптер у себя'), MapSection.nodeAlmatySub='KZ CHAPTER · ...' (ru: 'ЧАПТЕР KZ · ...'), Team.team5Role='Board · Events' (ru: 'Board · События'). This is a mistranslation pattern (leaving common nouns in English rather than translating them into Kazakh), not a legitimate domain-vocabulary exception, and directly contradicts the requirement's own decision text. SECONDARY (non-blocking on its own, but should be fixed in the same rework pass): Footer.licenseCode/licenseContent/licenseBrand keep the Russian words 'КОД'/'КОНТЕНТ'/'БРЕНД' verbatim -- these are plain nouns (code/content/brand), not names/codes/URLs/domain-vocabulary terms, so they do not qualify for the untranslatable-literal exception either (the license values themselves -- MIT, CC BY 4.0, AI QADAM BUP -- are legitimate literals and should stay).

issues.description: Domain-vocabulary rule misapplied in messages/kk.json: the requirement's decision says Event/Chapter/Talk/etc. stay in English only 'exactly as they already do in Russian... copy', but ru.json translates these words natively (событие, чаптер, доклад) except for CFP. kk.json instead substitutes literal English 'Event'/'Events'/'Chapter'/'Chapters'/'Talk' into nav labels, CTAs, eyebrows, titles, and body prose where ru.json uses native Russian vocabulary. Affected keys include Nav.events, Nav.chapters, Hero.ctaPrimary, Band.lede, Doors.door1Body, Doors.door2Link, Events.eyebrow, Streams.stream1Title, Partners.partner1Desc, MapSection.ctaLaunchChapter, MapSection.nodeAlmatySub, Team.team5Role.

Footer.licenseCode/licenseContent/licenseBrand leave the Russian plain nouns 'КОД'/'КОНТЕНТ'/'БРЕНД' untranslated. These are not domain-vocabulary terms or proper names -- only the trailing values (MIT, CC BY 4.0, AI QADAM BUP) are legitimate literals.

result.next_action: Rework CONTENT-BA: translate the Event/Chapter/Talk instances flagged above into native Kazakh (matching what ru.json actually does at each corresponding key -- only CFP is a genuine verbatim-English domain term in this dataset), and translate the Footer license-line labels (КОД/КОНТЕНТ/БРЕНД) into Kazakh, keeping the license values themselves (MIT, CC BY 4.0, AI QADAM BUP) verbatim.
